heroHeadline: Day 593: Yucatán Joins IMSS Bienestar as 24th State (Hospital O'Horán Inaugurated in Mérida); EU-Mexico Summit in 5 Days (May 22); First Sinaloa DOJ Indictee Arrested in Tucson
heroSubtitle: On May 17, 2026 (Day 593, Sunday), President Sheinbaum concluded her three-day Yucatán working tour with the marquee inauguration of the Hospital General 'Dr. Agustín O'Horán' of IMSS Bienestar in Mérida — described as the largest and most modern hospital in Latin America. The inauguration made Yucatán the 24th Mexican state to join IMSS Bienestar; starting May 18, all health services in Yucatán are free, with 183 medical units and 8 hospitals federalized. The O'Horán inauguration is the apex of a historic three-day tour that also produced the May 16 Tren Maya cargo groundbreaking at Puerto Progreso (26,200 jobs), the inauguration of the Hospital General Naval at Yucalpetén, Mexico's formal endorsement of Michelle Bachelet for UN Secretary-General, and the Sheinbaum-Trump 'cordial and excellent' phone call (with bilateral meeting set for ~May 27). On the sovereignty front: on May 16, retired General Gerardo Mérida Salgado — former Sinaloa public-security secretary and one of 10 officials indicted by the U.S. DOJ on April 29 — surrendered to U.S. federal agents in Tucson and was transferred to New York, becoming the first of the indicted officials to be apprehended. Sheinbaum's position remains firm: Mexico will not extradite Governor Rocha Moya without 'conclusive and irrefutable evidence,' citing the U.S.'s own rejection of 36 Mexican extradition requests. At her sovereignty address in Yucatán on May 17, Sheinbaum declared: 'Nada ni nadie va a detener la transformación de nuestra patria. Ningún gobierno extranjero le va a arrebatar la Transformación al pueblo de México.' Looking ahead: the EU-Mexico Summit on May 22 will formally sign the modernized EU-Mexico Global Agreement and Interim Trade Agreement with all 27 EU states — the first EU-Mexico summit in 11 years and a landmark trade diversification milestone. The first formal USMCA negotiating round is confirmed for the week of May 25, with U.S. envoys due in Mexico City around May 27.
